html:
Durdzuks is a medieval name, used mainly in Georgian sources from the 800s to the 1700s, for the Vainakh peoples, the ancestors of the Chechens and Ingush. They are on the map for 1100.

They lived in the mountain valleys of the central Caucasus, in clans with stone defence towers, and kept close ties with Georgia and with the Alans of the plains. The Mongols and later Timur attacked the region, and Islam spread there from the 1500s on. Their neighbours to the east were the Avars of Sarir. In 1944 Stalin deported the whole nation; see Chechens and Ingush deported.
